notes.title: Trenchfoot!
notes.notes: If you like old-school local multiplayer games Trenchfoot is hear to scratch your itch friend. It's the most exciting game you can have with friends and a gamepad. Come on an join the games creator for a couple of rounds of fun and frustration.

notes.title: Trenchfoot Update 1.0.1
notes.notes:
Update 1.0.1

Graphics:
This is the biggest change in the patch. The color pallet has changed significantly and a most sprites have been modified. 

Tweaks:
I've re-balanced the drop-rate of all powerups.

Bug fixes:
[list]
[*]Yet another bug-fix to the pipe system this should be the last bug.
[*]The block-kick needed a patch to fix kicking blocks through pipes.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 1.0 Release!
notes.notes:
This is the full release of Trenchfoot. 

New items:
[list]
[*] Added block kick
[*] Added speed down
[*] Added a bunch of new levels
[/list]

Fixes:
[list]
[*] There was an issue with the way pipes worked with explosions. This has been fixed
[*] Issue with kicking blocks into water / lava
[*] The controller library used has been updates and incorporated. This fixed a number of controll issues.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 0.7.8 Released: Lava, Block Kicking, New Effects, and Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
[b]This version adds:[/b]
[list]
[*] Block Kicking: Player placed blocks can be kicked if they are next to water or Lava. This fills in the water of lava tile, returning the space to regular ground.
[*] Lava: Lava kills players on contact, lava can be filled in by placing a block adjacent to a lava tile and kicking.
[*] Steam! if you place a lava tile on a water tile, or a water tile on a lava tile they will eliminate each other. This results in the lava or water tile becoming a regular tile.
[*] Environmental Effects System: This has been added and is currently being used to display lava bubbles.
[*] There are four new maps:
[list]
[*] [b]4 +[/b] : This map has rectangular rooms instead of the typical layout
[*] [b]4 x[/b] : This map has "X" shaped walls instead of the typical layout 
[*] [b]8 +[/b] : This map has rectangular rooms instead of the typical layout 
[*] [b]8 x[/b] : This map has "X" shaped walls instead of the typical layout 
[/list]
Feedback on these new maps is desperately needed. Please let me know what you think.
[/list]

[b]This version changes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Performance improvements. Specifically with explosions.
[/list]

[b]This version fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Title screen sound effect bug. This bug prevented the title screen sound effects from playing.
[*] Another explosion sound effect bug. This bug caused explosion sounds to play too quietly.
[*] Reinforced block bug. This bug allowed players to place bombs on the same tiles as reinforced blocks.
[*] Various pipe system issues. Fixed a number of pipe collision issues.
[/list]

[b]Color commentary:[/b]
I'm trying my best to make Trenchfoot the best party game it can be. Please, if you have any:
[list]
[*] Questions
[*] Comments
[*] Suggestions
[/list]

[b]Please contact me! You can reach me:[/b]
[list]
[*] On the Steam community forums: https://steamcommunity.com/app/793570
[*] On Discord: https://discord.gg/wqAk6nk
[*] Via email: trenchfeedback@cocompadres.com
[*] On Twitter: https://twitter.com/CoCompadresDev
[/list]
Let me know what you think! Help me make this the best party game possible!

notes.title: Happy Holidays! Trenchfoot Version 0.7.6 Released: Reinforced Walls, Tutorial, and Graphical Improvements
notes.notes:
Just in Time for Christmas! Version 0.7.6 features new content and the ability to reinforce blocks.

This version adds:
[list]
[*] Added new ability: Reinforcement. Players can reinforce blocks. Reinforced blocks cannot be destroyed by explosions. To reinforce a block:
[list]
[*] Place a regular block, then...
[*] While still standing on the regular block, place a block again.
Players can still destroy a reinforced block by walking into it, it will take a little longer to destroy it though.
[/list]
[*] A short and helpful tutorial has been added. This tutorial runs through:
[list]
[*] placing bombs
[*] detonating bombs
[*] placing blocks
[*] destroying blocks
[*] using blocks defensively
[/list]
[/list]

This version changes:
[list]
[*] This version includes a revised input system that:
[list]
[*] handles adding controllers better.
[*] adds the ability to use the right trigger button to detonate bombs [i]and[/i] place shapes.
[*] handles thumb-stick input better.
[/list] 
[*] The explosion graphics have been improved in this version
[/list]

Known Issues:
There is a known issue with the title screen. sometimes it does not select the correct option. Just exit back to the main menu and try again.

notes.title: Version 0.7.5.4 Released with Fences and Destroyable Pipes
notes.notes:
Version 0.7.5.4 features new content and the ability to destroy pipes

This version adds:
Added new tile type: Fences. Fences stop players, but do not impede explosions. 
Added new Ability: Destructible Pipes: This ability allows players to destroy pipes that have been placed.

This version fixes:
Some levels were missing timers. This has been fixed.

notes.title: Version 0.7.5.2 Released with Completed Pipe & Water System
notes.notes:
Version 0.7.5.2 features new content and a new and improved pipe and water system.

This version adds:
[list]
[*]Added new level "The Pond". With a large amount of unique water features.
[*]Added new Power-up: [b]Force Up[/b] increases the speed of explosions.
[/list]

This version Changes:
[list]
[*]Water and pipe tile graphics now appear connected.
[*]There is a new pipe system in place.
[*]Pipe shapes can now be placed anywhere. The engine will adjust them according to the surrounding tiles.
[*]Water shapes can now be placed anywhere and the engine will adjust them according to the surrounding tiles.
[/list]

This version fixes:
[list]
[*]Some levels were missing timers. This has been fixed.
[/list]

Color commentary:
Hidden from view are changes to the game's systems in general. This is the second "full game" I'm making. With the first one really being done to learn how to program, and get a tenuous grasp on how to work in Unity. In that sense it was successful, in every other sense it was not. I started this project because my awesome parents-in-law gave me a raspberry pi as a birthday present. As they gave it to me they said:

"Now you can make a game for it, and we can all play it when we're together again in December."

My birthday is in November. For those of you not familiar with the Gregorian calendar November is only one month away from December. I panicked as one is might expect, then I started considering options.

[list]
[*]I wanted the game to be fun.
[*]I wanted it to support multiple players locally.
[*]I wanted it to be easy for beginners to pick up, as my in-laws are not gamers. More importantly, I wanted the game to be enjoyable in a family/party setting with players of different skill levels.
[*]I wanted the game to be appropriate for all ages. Again I wanted it to be enjoyable in a family setting.
[*]I needed to have an MVP ready in a month. Working on it while I had school and a very busy work schedule.
[/list]

This was how Code name Pop-pals started.

notes.title: Version 0.7.5.1 Released with Features from PAX Feedback
notes.notes:
Version 0.7.5.1 with features requested by users who played the game at PAX. The features added in this version are focused for the most part on usability.

This version adds:
[list]
[*]Added a graphic and an animation that points to where the player respawns after they place a shape.
[*]Added shape controls to the controller pause graphic.
[*]Changed the graphics and added an animation for the remote bomb.
[*]Added a countdown timer at the top of the screen.
[/list]

This version Changes:
[list]
[*]Shortened all round durations.
[*]All "PAX Patch" levels are timed. None of them are based on player deaths.
[/list]

This version fixes:
[list]
[*]Sound bug where large explosions would stop playing explosion sound.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 0.7.5 Released - Final PAX Patch
notes.notes:
Version 0.7.5 includes fixes and changes made due to feedback and bugs found at PAX.

This version adds:
[list]
[*]Added the ability to destroy blocks that are currently placed below you. Simply press the bomb button 4 times and you will destroy the block. This allows you to place a bomb where the block was previously.
[*]Adds maps for 6, 10, 12, and 14 player matches. This is in addition to the original 4, 8, and 16 player maps.
[/list]

This version Changes:
[list]
[*]16 Player map is larger now.
[*]Changed initial starting locations on all maps so players start closer to each other.
[*]Time limits on all maps are now customized to the size of the map.
[/list]

This version fixes:
[list]
[*]Players getting stuck between pipes.
[*]Players being able to kick bombs through the sides of pipe entrances.
[*]Scoreboards not subtracting self kills correctly.
[*]The pipes in Pipe's Place Roast.
[/list]

notes.title: Trenchfoot version 0.7.0 Released!
notes.notes:
This new version has added the ability for players that have been bombed to place a randomly generated set of blocks anywhere valid on the map. This is a big change and it's not fully implemented yet, but it should make for some unique fun and dynamic moments.

In addition to the pipes tiles released in version 0.6.3, update 0.7.0 adds another tile type. Water tiles prevent explosions from expanding past them, but they do not hinder player movement. 

This release is big release, so have fun!

notes.title: Trenchfoot released for early access!
notes.notes:
I just released Trenchfoot for early access, the game is still a little rough around the edges. It needs some graphics work, there are more power-ups and abilities I will be adding down the road, I'm still looking for music, and working on the sound effects. That being said the core gameplay is very solid, the game does support 8-players locally and there are 3 interesting new bombs in the game that are really fun to play with.

I hope you enjoy it, and I would greatly appreciate any and all feedback.


Thanks,
-matt
